title: The ₩150,000 I Held Back
description:
{name} once held back an impulse buy, thinking 'before ₩3 billion, even ₩150,000 has to be saved.'

Those small saved amounts piled up.

Today they stood before a similar temptation.

choices.text: Like then — small restraint stacks into the goal
choices.result_text:
₩150,000 doesn't make ₩3 billion. But the habit of restraint does.

The one who can hold back is the one who ends up saving.
{name} closed the wallet again today. A small victory.

choices.text: Now, sometimes — spend on myself too
choices.result_text:
Hold back everything and something eventually bursts.

{name} learned the balance between restraint and reward.
To finish five years, you have to allow yourself small things sometimes.

title: Memories Are an Asset, I Said
description:
{name} once consoled themselves the morning after an impulse buy — 'memories are an asset.'

How is that spending's memory now?

Today they stood before a similar choice.

choices.text: That memory's still good — experience is investment too
choices.result_text:
Spend all money only on the future and the present disappears.

That experience became a small breathing hole for {name}.
They just know how to control the frequency now.

choices.text: A bank balance reassures more than memories — restraint now
choices.result_text:
That rationalization wasn't always right.

{name} decided not to hide behind 'experience is an asset.'
The real asset was a balance edging closer to the goal.

title: The Vow Never to Do It Again
description:
{name} once regretted an impulse buy the next day, vowing 'never again, focus on the goal.'

Was that vow kept?

Today the impulse returns.

choices.text: Thanks to that regret — spending habits took hold
choices.result_text:
Regret matters only when it changes the next action.

That regret matured {name}'s spending one notch.
One who learns from a mistake repeats it less.

choices.text: Check whether I only regretted and repeated
choices.result_text:
Regret and change are different.

{name} honestly examined whether they'd only repeated vows.
What truly changed wasn't the count of vows, but the results of actions.

title: Envying the Choice Not to Marry
description:
To a friend who declared they'd stay single, {name} said, 'I envy you — that decision couldn't have been easy.'

That conversation comes back sometimes.

Today thoughts of marriage and singlehood cross the mind again.

choices.text: Married or single — it's my choice to make
choices.result_text:
Envy another's decision too long and you fail to make your own.

{name} settled that neither marriage nor singlehood is the answer — it's a personal choice.
What matters isn't a path assigned by others, but one you choose.

choices.text: Goal first for now — think about it after
choices.result_text:
No need to decide everything at once.

{name} decided to focus on the current goal first.
Life's big decisions aren't too late to face once there's some room.

title: Alone Is Enough, I Said
description:
{name} once enjoyed their freedom and felt 'alone is enough.'

Is that peace still valid?

In a quiet room today, that feeling returned.

choices.text: Even now — solitary time fills me
choices.result_text:
Not enduring time alone, but enjoying it.

That capacity made {name} sturdier.
Loneliness and solitude differ. Solitude was a self-chosen fullness.

choices.text: Enough, yes — but sometimes I miss company
choices.result_text:
Alone being enough didn't mean needing no one.

{name} acknowledged both self-sufficiency and the longing for connection.
The two weren't a contradiction, but two natural sides of a person.

title: Deleting the App, Calling Comparison a Thief
description:
{name} once deleted the SNS app, saying 'comparison is a thief.'

They hadn't looked at others' feeds since.

Today they happened to hear someone's glamorous update.

choices.text: Glad I deleted it — my time became mine
choices.result_text:
What comparison steals is time and composure.

After deleting the app, {name} reclaimed those stolen things.
Just not comparing others' highlights to one's daily life lightened the heart.

choices.text: Now I'm unshaken even seeing it — I've grown sturdy
choices.result_text:
Deleting the app was training, not escape.

Now {name}'s pace doesn't waver even seeing others' boasts.
Past the avoiding stage, arrived at the stage of being fine facing it.

title: Stimulation Can Be Motivation, I Said
description:
{name} once kept watching SNS, saying 'stimulation can be motivation.'

Did that comparison become motivation, or poison?

Today, scrolling the feed, the mind grew complicated again.

choices.text: Now I know — comparison was more poison than motivation
choices.result_text:
Believed it'd be stimulating, but mostly it just gnawed at the heart.

{name} now knows comparison's real cost.
Motivation lasted longer coming from within, not from others' feeds.

choices.text: I learned to turn comparison into fuel
choices.result_text:
The same comparison can sink you or lift you.

{name} learned to turn envy into analysis.
Start asking 'how did they do it?' and comparison becomes study.

title: The First Reward to Myself
description:
{name} once bought their first luxury item, calling it 'a first reward to myself.'

That item is still around.

Looking at it today, that feeling came back.

choices.text: That reward had meaning — it acknowledged me
choices.result_text:
A life of only holding back doesn't last.

That first reward wasn't extravagance, but recognition of the self who'd come this far.
{name} didn't regret it. Sometimes that's needed.

choices.text: More than the item — the sense of achievement was real
choices.result_text:
More than the luxury itself, the fact of having come far enough to buy it was bigger.

{name} also knows an item's satisfaction is short.
The real reward was in the journey, not the bank account.

title: Just Taking a Photo and Leaving
description:
{name} once left a luxury store with just a photo, thinking 'not yet.'

That moment of restraint comes back sometimes.

Today they stood before a similar temptation.

choices.text: Holding back then — narrowed the distance now
choices.result_text:
Those photo-only moments gathered into seed money.

Holding back wasn't penny-pinching — it was a choice.
{name} wasn't ashamed of that restraint. It was restraint with a goal.

choices.text: Now — if I truly want it, I can buy it
choices.result_text:
Always holding back isn't the answer.

{name} now knows how to spend on what's truly wanted.
Restraint and stinginess differ. Spending with discernment was a skill too.

title: I Have My Own Pace, I Said
description:
When a friend bought an imported car, {name} genuinely congratulated them, saying 'I have my own pace.'

That composure comes back sometimes.

Today they faced another display of someone's success.

choices.text: Even now — I'm not swayed by others' speed
choices.result_text:
A friend buying a car doesn't mean I've fallen behind.

There are only different games, different timetables.
{name} knows that composure ultimately took them farther.

choices.text: My turn comes too — quietly prepare
choices.result_text:
Instead of envying now, build silently.

{name} knows it's a time to prepare, not to show off.
When the quiet accumulation ends, it shows without needing to boast.

title: The Sting I Felt
description:
When a friend bought an imported car, {name} felt a sting — 'what am I even doing?'

What became of that envy?

A similar moment came today.

choices.text: I've turned that sting into fuel
choices.result_text:
Envy doesn't vanish by ignoring it. Given direction, it becomes fuel.

{name} used that sting to rise instead of sink.
Comparison is poison, but handled well it becomes medicine.

choices.text: It stings less now — because I see my path
choices.result_text:
Before, another's car stung. Now less so.

The clearer one's own path, the less others' speed mattered.
{name} knows that change is itself growth.

title: Breathing for One Night
description:
{name} once took a hotel staycation, saying 'sometimes you have to breathe.'

That one night of rest comes back sometimes.

Today is the end of another exhausting day.

choices.text: That rest — gave me the strength to run again
choices.result_text:
The money spent on rest might feel wasteful. But that one night prevented burnout.

Rest was an investment, not a cost.
{name} knows that letting yourself rest is a skill too.

choices.text: Now I know how to rest more cheaply too
choices.result_text:
You can rest without a hotel.

{name} learned to recover spending less.
The essence of rest wasn't the place, but the heart that pauses for a moment.

title: Saying Proudly: I Have a Goal
description:
Asked why they were frugal, {name} once answered proudly, 'because I have a goal.'

That pride comes back sometimes.

Today someone again puzzles over {name}'s thriftiness.

choices.text: Still proud — it's strategy, not penny-pinching
choices.result_text:
Frugality for a goal is nothing to be ashamed of.

Even if others see penny-pinching, {name} knows it's their own choice.
Proud frugality was the mark of someone unshaken.

choices.text: No need to explain — show it with results
choices.result_text:
The more you explain, the more it sounds like an excuse.

{name} decided to prove it with results instead of words.
Once arrived, what the frugality was for becomes clear without saying.

title: Sitting at That Table
description:
{name} once joined a golf gathering, saying 'there are things you only see seated at that table.'

That networking table comes back sometimes.

Today they were invited to a similar gathering.

choices.text: I learned something there — I'll go again
choices.result_text:
Some information and opportunities flow only at such tables.

{name} knows the value of sitting there even when uncomfortable.
Networking is a cost, but used well it's the fastest shortcut.

choices.text: Now I pick my tables — not every seat is the answer
choices.result_text:
Not every networking table helps.

{name} learned to tell which to attend and which to skip.
Time is an asset too, so where to spend it was itself strategy.
